 Tyler Herro (leg) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Herro injured his leg during Sunday’s loss to the Celtics and will not play on Tuesday. Herro’s absence could mean Ryan Rollins returns to the starting lineup, raising his fantasy ceiling.

 Ryan Rollins 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #13 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Ryan Rollins amassed 14 points (5-of-9 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 The Bucks didn’t have Tyler Herro for Tuesday’s game, so Rollins made his first start since Halloween. While the production was solid, he logged 24 minutes, with Kasparas Jakučionis (11 points, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers) playing 23 minutes off the bench. If Herro remains out for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers, Rollins may still have some value in 12-team leagues. That said, his recent move to the bench and reduced minutes are a major concern for managers who selected Rollins with a middle-round pick. 
 Ryan Rollins 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #13 
 Ryan Rollins, Brayden Burries, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner will start Tuesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 The Bucks won’t have Tyler Herro for Tuesday’s game, as he’s out with a leg injury. Rollins returns to the starting lineup for the first time since Halloween, which raises his short-term fantasy ceiling. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Tyler Herro (leg) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Herro suffered an injury scare during Sunday’s loss to the Celtics but returned to the game after a quick trip to the locker room. If he can’t play on Tuesday, Ryan Rollins could return to the starting lineup after being replaced by rookie Brayden Burries. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Tyler Herro delivered a team-high 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, 10 assists and one steal over 35 minutes in a loss to the Raptors on Friday. 
 Herro has been one of the more consistent, upper-echelon scoring threats in the league this season, averaging a cool 22 points per-game. This was a rare off-night from long range as he connected on just 1-of-5 from downtown after shooting over 40 percent through the first eight games of the year. There’s almost zero competition for shots in Milwaukee, which means that Herro should have the green light any time he’s on the floor. 
 Ryan Rollins 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #13 
 Ryan Rollins accounted for 13 points (5-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Celtics. 
 Coming off the bench for a second straight game, Rollins played seven more minutes than he did in Monday’s loss to the Timberwolves. His final line against the Celtics was solid, with four turnovers being the only issue. However, while the increased playing time is encouraging, the Bucks’ pivot to lottery pick Brayden Burries (9/5/3/1 in 22 minutes) is concerning for fantasy managers who used a middle-round pick on Rollins. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Tyler Herro finished Wednesday’s loss to the Celtics with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers. 
 Over eight games, things have gone the way many fantasy managers hoped for regarding Herro. He’s scored 21+ points on six occasions and is providing fifth-round value in 12-team leagues. Herro didn’t record any steals against the Celtics, but he’s averaging one per game this season. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Tyler Herro had 21 points (8-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, three steals and four three-pointers against the Timberwolves on Monday. 
 Herro was hardly efficient on Monday with 21 points on 18 attempts. He made four three-pointers and added three steals on the defensive end. Herro has scored at least 21 points in five of seven games with the Bucks to start the season. Milwaukee will travel to Boston for a road matchup against the Celtics Wednesday. 
 Brayden Burries 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Brayden Burries, Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner will start against the Timberwolves on Monday. 
 Burries will get the first start of his career, with Ryan Rollins heading to the bench. There isn’t any injury reason for Rollins to head to the bench, so this could be a permanent move, which would bode well for Burries’ value. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Tyler Herro finished Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers with 15 points (5-of-18 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers. 
 This wasn’t Herro’s best night, as he shot 1-of-7 from inside the arc. While the four three-pointers will please some fantasy managers, the overall output was disappointing. However, given the gap between the Bucks and Cavaliers, it wasn’t all that surprising. Herro will look to bounce back on Monday when the Bucks visit the Timberwolves. Milwaukee plays four games next week. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Tyler Herro had 23 points (9-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Herro has scored at least 23 points and made at least three three-pointers in four of five games so far this season. He played 27 minutes in a game the Bucks lost by 32. Given Milwaukee’s lack of depth, which has led to high usage for Herro, the only thing that can slow him down are blowouts.

 Isaiah Collier produced 17 points (5-of-10 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Heat.
 While Keyonte George’s ankle injury did not result in a start for Collier, his role did take on added importance. The Jazz guard had an efficient night, shooting 4-of-4 from three and committing two turnovers before fouling out. If George misses more time, Collier will be worth a look in deep leagues, even if his shooting against the Heat wasn’t his norm.

 Ace Bailey accounted for 23 points (10-of-15 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Heat.
 Bailey enjoyed one of the best offensive performances of his young NBA career on Tuesday. Shooting 66.7 percent from the field, the second-year forward finished with a season-high 23 points. After scoring at least 20 points in 16 games as a rookie, this was his first 20-point game of the 2026-27 campaign. Already without Jaren Jackson Jr., the Jazz didn’t have Lauri Markkanen on Tuesday, and those absences have raised Bailey’s short-term ceiling. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darryn Peterson finished Tuesday’s loss to the Heat with 25 points (10-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
 With no Keyonte George, Peterson made his first start at point guard for the Jazz on Tuesday. While he committed five turnovers and ultimately fouled out, this was a good night overall for the rookie. Peterson scored efficiently and dished out a few assists in his 31 minutes. His fantasy ceiling should be raised slightly for as long as George remains sidelined.

 Pelle Larsson accounted for 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz.
 Larsson has started Miami’s last two games, recording solid stat lines in each. The question worth considering is whether this move will stick for the long haul, or only as long as it takes Andrew Wiggins to find his offensive form. Against the Jazz, Wiggins scored 13 points on 5-of-8 shooting but did not record any other stats. Even with his reserve role at the start of the season, Larsson has been the superior fantasy option.

 Davion Mitchell recorded 19 points (5-of-13 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz.
 The dilemma for fantasy managers rostering Mitchell: sell high or hold? “Off Night” has been highly productive for the Heat this season, and Miami’s lack of depth at point guard means he’ll play heavy minutes. However, those who aren’t convinced Mitchell can play at this level for a full season should strongly consider looking into what he could fetch in a trade. Mitchell finished Tuesday’s victory two assists shy of a double-double, making up for the low field-goal percentage.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 30 points (12-of-21 FGs, 5-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz.
 Initially questionable for Tuesday’s game with a sprained right wrist, Antetokounmpo got up 21 shots against the Jazz. He scored 15 points in each half, shooting 7-of-14 from the field in the second half. Giannis’ dominant performance helped offset Bam Adebayo’s (11/8/4/4/2) 1-of-8 shooting from the field. The Heat head home, with a Friday/Saturday back-to-back against the Cavaliers and Pistons up next.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Suns.
 While not a player who absolutely has to be rostered in 12-team leagues, Jones has been productive enough to provide reliable deep-league value. Against the Suns, his final stat line lacked only an assist, and he’s now shooting 17-of-36 from beyond the arc. Jones would help his fantasy value if he could consistently provide steals; six of his 10 steals this season have been recorded in two games.

 Rui Hachimura tallied 13 points (4-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Suns.
 Hachimura shot 3-of-5 from beyond the arc on Tuesday, and the two steals matched his season high. Unfortunately, his production outside of points and rebounds remains limited, and the Clippers forward is shooting below 40 percent from the field. Hachimura’s status as a starter is why he’s rostered in 62 percent of Yahoo leagues, but that number may decrease once Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is cleared to play.
